claims.statement: Graph-attached RF engines derive from ComponentEngineBase, which owns graph identity, SignalNode storage, and single-input dirty checking; two-input engines must track both input generations independently.

ComponentTypeRegistry defines 13 graph-attached engine descriptors with canonical and project keys, fields, capabilities, and factories; its authorable flag selects only the subset offered by the New Component form. Spectrum and Network Analyzers are separate instruments, not graph registry components.

The ADC engine contract uses fs_Hz, nsd_dBm_per_Hz, decimation, and nco_fs_fraction, with sample-rate, supported-decimation, and NCO-fraction bounds enforced by its setters; legacy bits and v_fs are not engine parameters.

RF processing engines implement distinct models: the amplifier applies S21 to tones and models gain, noise figure, and optional nonlinearity; the mixer exposes LO frequency, conversion gain, and noise figure; the ideal filter selects LPF, HPF, BPF, or BSF; the equalizer applies a slope or S21; the attenuator takes attenuation_dB or S-parameter data; and the coax cable models cable length and connector loss.

The splitter applies a fixed 3.0103 dB loss to each output, and manual Combiner mode applies the same loss to each input tone path and incoherently sums noise; in three-port S-parameter mode the combiner maps S21 and S31 and adds only non-negative passive thermal noise.

The two RF SPDT orientations serialize an integer active-throw index with insertion/isolation losses, accept T1/T2 names from component-library authoring, apply insertion loss on the selected path and isolation loss on the other, and track each output or both inputs as appropriate.

PFBChannelizerEngine has one input and two indexed outputs: output 0 is the active channel view and output 1 is the reconstructed full spectrum. It defaults to critical sampling, persists ratios 1x/2x, and sets channel output Fs to ratio times input Fs divided by M; 2x widens channel bandwidth without moving channel centers.

SpectrumAnalyzerEngine is not a graph engine; it separates per-bin noise and tone power for RBW processing, caches that work by spectrum pointer, generation, RBW, and bin width, applies VBW and optional noise-only jitter every frame, and keys trace histories by Spectrum pointer. Its widget exposes RBW and VBW over 1 kHz to 100 MHz in kHz, while the engine setters stay unclamped.

The Network Analyzer is a non-component instrument that measures the forward chain between its two output pins on private scratch clones driven by a synthetic tone comb, preserving exact ports; it reports unavailable results as NaN and skips recomputation when the path signature and sweep settings are unchanged.

Spectrum noise is represented as power spectral density in W/Hz across the signal chain, so passive stages scale noise by power gain and add thermal contributions while ADC uses configured NSD and active stages use NF-derived additions.

Component-library definitions are validated at the load boundary: ComponentLibrary::validate checks registry fields and enum values, and definitions with type, range, or enum issues are rejected before they reach the insertion UI or the engine factory. Canonical keys include attenuation_dB, conversion_gain_dB, and the RF-switch active_throw values T1 and T2.

The runtime enforces the ADC-only PFB input rule before committing a link and when restoring project links: only ADC output 0 to PFB input 0 is permitted, and a direct RF generator-to-PFB link is rejected.

PFB channel noise and ENBW are integrated on the current input grid using the squared channel response and input-bin width, and the inspector presents the active-channel noise in dBm with effective ENBW.

PFB node-hover SNR compares the strongest active-channel tone against integrated channel noise independently of analyzer RBW, while ordinary component hover SNR uses the Spectrum Analyzer's RBW-based strongest-tone measurement.

utils::inputDouble and utils::inputFrequency limit user edits rather than displayed values: an engine value outside the limits is shown as is, flagged amber with a tooltip, and logged once; a user edit clamps into the limits, is ignored when clamping would reverse it, and commits nothing when it leaves the value unchanged.
